meta.title: Which House Claims You?
meta.instructions: Brambleford Academy's Lantern sorts every new student into one of four houses. Eight questions: answer on instinct before your candle burns down. Hesitate twice and it goes dark, and a split heart can't be sorted. Then send your crest to the group chat.

top_house.body: fold(range(4), 0, (b, h) => if get_or(tally, h, 0) > get_or(tally, b, 0) then h else b)

runner_up.body: let t = top_house() in fold(range(4), if t == 0 then 1 else 0, (b, h) => if h != t and get_or(tally, h, 0) > get_or(tally, b, 0) then h else b)

candle_frac.body: if phase != 'ask' then 0.0 else if now < asked_at + 1500 then 1.0 else max(0.0, 1.0 - (now - asked_at - 1500) * 1.0 / 9000.0)

glow.body: let top = max(1, max_of(tally)) in 0.28 + 0.72 * min(1.0, get_or(tally, h, 0) * 1.0 / top)

breakdown.body: join(map(sort_by(range(4), h => 0 - get_or(tally, h, 0)), h => get_or(content_emoji, h, '') + ' ' + str(get_or(tally, h, 0))), '   ')

template.opacity: = if phase == 'ask' and now < asked_at + 1500 then 0.45 else if phase == 'chosen' and picked != k then 0.35 else 1.0

children.fill: = if phase == 'chosen' and picked == k then '#F5C66B40' else '#00000000'
children.stroke: = if phase == 'chosen' and picked == k then '#F5C66B' else '#00000000'

children.text: The Lantern can’t read a split heart. Brambleford only sorts the decisive. Answer again, with conviction.

questions: First night at Brambleford, your dorm door locks itself from the outside. You…
You post in the group chat. Nobody replies for an hour. You…
The Midnight Exam is tomorrow. Tonight you…
A cursed mirror shows your worst habit. It's…
A friend is crying in the library. You…
Your house wins the Lantern Cup. You celebrate by…
choices: Pick the lock with a hairpin and a half-remembered spell
Slide a note under the door. Someone always answers notes.
Recite Rule 41 (no door may lock a student in) until it opens
Knock and offer the hallway ghost half your biscuit
A moth who only flies toward bad ideas
A toad with strong opinions about your essays
An owl who keeps your secrets, and a few of her own
A round hedgehog who naps in your teacup
Post again. Louder. With a gif.
Screenshot it. For the records.
Quietly check on the friend who's been off lately
Send a photo of the soup you just made for everyone
Study by candlelight in the bell tower, alone
Find out who wrote the exam. Find their notes.
Make flashcards for your whole corridor
Sleep. You'll improvise. You always do.
Saying 'one more chapter' at 3 a.m.
Correcting a rival's spell pronunciation mid-duel
Saying yes to every plan, then inventing three more
Adopting every stray. Every. Single. One.
A thundercloud, barely contained
A rival's annotated notes, 'borrowed' indefinitely
Midnight-blue velvet that smells like rain
A patchwork quilt your gran stitched for luck
Sit beside them without a word. Pass tissues.
Ask who did it. Open a file. Start a plan.
Announce a midnight kitchen raid. Right now.
Wrap them in your coat. Tea is already brewing.
Watching the fireworks from the roof, grinning
Climbing the clock tower to ring the bell yourself
Writing a twelve-page account of exactly why you won
Baking a cake shaped like the cup, for everyone
mottos: “Jump first. Plan on the way down.”
“Read the fine print. Then rewrite it.”
blurbs: You notice everything and say half of it. You're the friend people text at 2 a.m., and you always answer.
You start the fun and finish the stories. Curfew is a dare, and somehow everyone gets home safe because you were there.
You read the rules to find the loopholes. You win arguments three days later, and your notes beat the teacher's.
You remember birthdays, allergies and everyone's tea order. Your room is where the group ends up. Soft heart, iron spine.
